celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿يَا مُوسَى إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the matter (al-shaʾn) ﴿أَنَا اللَّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ﴾ so he threw it down ﴿فَلَمَّا رَآهَا تَهْتَزُّ﴾ moving ﴿كَأَنَّهَا جَانٌّ﴾ a light, nimble snake ﴿وَلَّى مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ﴾ he did not turn back. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿يَا مُوسَى لَا تَخَفْ﴾ of it ﴿إِنِّي لَا يَخَافُ لَدَيَّ﴾ in My presence ﴿الْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾ of a snake or anything else.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ i.e. but (lākin) ﴿مَنْ ظَلَمَ﴾ himself ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْنًا﴾ which he did ﴿بَعْدَ سُوءٍ﴾ i.e. he repented ﴿فَإِنِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ I accept repentance and forgive him.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ﴾ the collar-opening of the shirt ﴿تَخْرُجْ﴾ contrary to its colour of brownness ﴿بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ﴾ leprosy, having a radiance that dazzles the sight, as a sign ﴿فِي تِسْعِ آيَاتٍ﴾ sent with them ﴿إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمًا فَاسِقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَتْهُمْ آيَاتُنَا مُبْصِرَةً﴾ i.e. shining and clear ﴿قَالُوا هَذَا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ evident and manifest.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَجَحَدُوا بِهَا﴾ i.e. they did not acknowledge them ﴿وَ﴾ [while] indeed (qad) ﴿اسْتَيْقَنَتْهَا أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ they were certain that they were from Allah ﴿ظُلْمًا وَعُلُوًّا﴾ arrogance towards believing in what Moses brought; [these two words] refer back to the denial ﴿فَانْظُرْ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾ which you have come to know, namely their destruction.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا دَاوُدَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ﴾ his son ﴿عِلْمًا﴾ of judging between people, of the speech of birds and other things ﴿وَقَالَا﴾ in thanks to Allah ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي فَضَّلَنَا﴾ with prophethood and the subjugation of jinn, humans and devils ﴿عَلَى كَثِيرٍ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمَانُ دَاوُدَ﴾ prophethood and knowledge, to the exclusion of the rest of his children ﴿وَقَالَ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ عُلِّمْنَا مَنْطِقَ الطَّيْرِ﴾ i.e. understanding their sounds ﴿وَأُوتِينَا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ that prophets and kings are given ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا﴾ which has been given ﴿لَهُوَ الْفَضْلُ الْمُبِينُ﴾ the clear, manifest [favour].

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَحُشِرَ﴾ were gathered ﴿لِسُلَيْمَانَ جُنُودُهُ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ وَالطَّيْرِ﴾ on a journey of his ﴿فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ﴾ they are gathered, then driven along.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا أَتَوْا عَلَى وَادِ النَّمْلِ﴾ it is at al-Ṭāʾif or in Syria (al-Shām); its ants are small or large ﴿قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ﴾ the queen of the ants, having seen Solomon's army ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَسَاكِنَكُمْ لَا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ﴾ crush you ﴿سُلَيْمَانُ وَجُنُودُهُ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ the ants were treated as rational beings in being addressed with the form of address used for them.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿فَتَبَسَّمَ﴾ Solomon, at first ﴿ضَاحِكًا﴾ in the end ﴿مِنْ قَوْلِهَا﴾ he had heard it from three miles away, the wind carrying it to him; so he held back his army when he came upon their valley until they had entered their homes. His army on this journey were riders and men on foot. ﴿وَقَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي﴾ inspire me ﴿أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ﴾ with it ﴿عَلَيَّ وَعَلَى وَالِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَالِحًا تَرْضَاهُ وَأَدْخِلْنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِي عِبَادِكَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ the prophets and the saints (awliyāʾ).

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَتَفَقَّدَ الطَّيْرَ﴾ to see the hoopoe, which sees water beneath the earth and points to it by pecking there, whereupon the devils draw it out, because Solomon needed it for prayer; but he did not see it ﴿فَقَالَ مَا لِيَ لَا أَرَى الْهُدْهُدَ﴾ i.e. has something befallen me that prevents me from seeing it? ﴿أَمْ كَانَ مِنَ الْغَائِبِينَ﴾ so that I did not see it because of its absence. When he had confirmed its absence, he said:

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿لَأُعَذِّبَنَّهُ عَذَابًا﴾ a punishment (taʿdhīb) ﴿شَدِيدًا﴾ by plucking its feathers and its tail and casting it into the sun, so that it cannot protect itself from vermin ﴿أَوْ لَأَذْبَحَنَّهُ﴾ by cutting its throat ﴿أَوْ لَيَأْتِيَنِّي﴾ with a doubled nūn with kasra, or [a nūn] with fatḥa followed by a nūn with kasra ﴿بِسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ with a clear, manifest proof for its excuse.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿فَمَكُثَ﴾ with ḍamma on the kāf and with fatḥa [فَمَكَثَ] ﴿غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ﴾ i.e. a short time; and it presented itself to Solomon humbly, raising its head and lowering its tail and wings, so he pardoned it and asked it about what it had met with during its absence ﴿فَقَالَ أَحَطْتُ بِمَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ﴾ i.e. I have come to know what you have not come to know ﴿وَجِئْتُكَ مِنْ سَبَإٍ﴾ with nunation (ṣarf) and without it; a tribe in Yemen named after an ancestor of theirs, and in view of that it is nunated ﴿بِنَبَإٍ﴾ news ﴿يَقِينٍ﴾.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿إِنِّي وَجَدْتُ امْرَأَةً تَمْلِكُهُمْ﴾ i.e. she is a queen over them, her name being Bilqīs ﴿وَأُوتِيَتْ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ that kings need of equipment and provisions ﴿وَلَهَا عَرْشٌ﴾ a throne ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾ its length eighty cubits, its breadth forty cubits and its height thirty cubits, wrought of gold and silver, crowned with pearls, red rubies, green chrysolite and emeralds, and its legs of red rubies; over it are seven doors, on every chamber a locked door.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَجَدْتُهَا وَقَوْمَهَا يَسْجُدُونَ لِلشَّمْسِ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ the path of truth ﴿فَهُمْ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿أَلَّا يَسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ﴾ i.e. that they should prostrate to Him; lā was added and the nūn of an was assimilated into it, as in His saying {لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ}. The clause is in the position of the object of يَهْتَدُونَ by dropping إِلَى ﴿الَّذِي يُخْرِجُ الْخَبْءَ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of what is hidden (al-makhbūʾ), of rain and plants ﴿فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا يُخْفُونَ﴾ in their hearts, and what

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿يُعْلِنُونَ﴾ with their tongues ﴿اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾ resumptive (istiʾnāf): a clause of praise containing [mention of] the Throne of the All-Merciful as against the throne of Bilqīs, and between the two there is an immense difference.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Solomon to the hoopoe ﴿سَنَنْظُرُ أَصَدَقْتَ﴾ in what you have told us ﴿أَمْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ﴾ i.e. of this kind [of people]; this is more emphatic than "or did you lie about it". Then it guided them to water, which was drawn out, and they drank their fill, performed ablution and prayed. Then Solomon wrote a letter whose form was: "From the servant of Allah, Solomon son of David, to Bilqīs, queen of Sheba: In the name of Allah, the All-Merciful, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon whoever follows guidance. To proceed: do not exalt yourselves against me, and come to me in submission (muslimīn)." Then he sealed it with musk and stamped it with his seal-ring, then said to the hoopoe:

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿اذْهَبْ بِكِتَابِي هَذَا فَأَلْقِهْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. Bilqīs and her people ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ﴾ turn away ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ and stand near them ﴿فَانْظُرْ مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ what reply they return. So it took it and came to her while her troops were around her and dropped it into her lap. When she saw it she trembled and was humbled in fear; then she read what was in it; then

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿قَالَتْ﴾ to the nobles of her people ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ إِنِّي﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully (taḥqīq) and with the second softened (tashīl) by changing it into a wāw with kasra ﴿أُلْقِيَ إِلَيَّ كِتَابٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ sealed.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ مِنْ سُلَيْمَانَ وَإِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. its content ﴿بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾

celaleyn:31-31.t:
﴿أَلَّا تَعْلُوا عَلَيَّ وَأْتُونِي مُسْلِمِينَ﴾
[Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿قَالَتْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِي﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully and with the second softened by changing it into a wāw; i.e. advise me ﴿فِي أَمْرِي مَا كُنْتُ قَاطِعَةً أَمْرًا﴾ deciding it ﴿حَتَّى تَشْهَدُونِ﴾ you are present.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿قَالُوا نَحْنُ أُولُو قُوَّةٍ وَأُولُوا بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾ i.e. people of might in war ﴿وَالْأَمْرُ إِلَيْكِ فَانْظُرِي مَاذَا تَأْمُرِينَ﴾ "-nā" [us], we will obey you. [Translator's note: the source reads «نَا نُطِعْكِ», apparently the end of «تَأْمُرِينَنَا نُطِعْكِ» "what you command us, we will obey you".]

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿قَالَتْ إِنَّ الْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُوا قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا﴾ by laying waste ﴿وَجَعَلُوا أَعِزَّةَ أَهْلِهَا أَذِلَّةً وَكَذَلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ i.e. the senders of the letter.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿وَإِنِّي مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِمْ بِهَدِيَّةٍ فَنَاظِرَةٌ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ الْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾ whether accepting the gift or rejecting it: if he is a king he will accept it, and if a prophet he will not accept it. So she sent servants, male and female, a thousand in equal number, and five hundred bricks of gold, a crown studded with jewels, musk, ambergris and other things, with an envoy carrying a letter. The hoopoe hastened to Solomon to tell him the news, so he ordered that bricks of gold and silver be struck and laid out from where he was for nine parasangs (farsakh) as a courtyard, that they build around it a crenellated wall of gold and silver, and that the finest beasts of land and sea be brought, together with the children of the jinn, to the right and left of the courtyard.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَ﴾ the envoy with the gift, accompanied by his followers ﴿سُلَيْمَانَ قَالَ أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بِمَالٍ فَمَا آتَانِيَ اللَّهُ﴾ of prophethood and kingship ﴿خَيْرٌ مِمَّا آتَاكُمْ﴾ of this world ﴿بَلْ أَنْتُمْ بِهَدِيَّتِكُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ﴾ because of your pride in the ornaments of this world.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿ارْجِعْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ with the gift you brought ﴿فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّهُمْ بِجُنُودٍ لَا قِبَلَ﴾ no power ﴿لَهُمْ بِهَا وَلَنُخْرِجَنَّهُمْ مِنْهَا﴾ from their land, Sheba, named after the father of their tribe ﴿أَذِلَّةً وَهُمْ صَاغِرُونَ﴾ i.e. if they do not come to me in submission. When the envoy returned to her with the gift, she placed her throne within seven doors inside her palace, and her palace was within seven palaces; the doors were locked and she set guards over them, and she prepared to travel to Solomon to see what he would command her. So she set out with twelve thousand chieftains (qayl), with each chieftain many thousands, until she came within a parasang of him; he became aware of her

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿قَالَ يَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَيُّكُمْ﴾ regarding the two hamzas, what has preceded [applies] ﴿يَأْتِينِي بِعَرْشِهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ يَأْتُونِي مُسْلِمِينَ﴾ submissive and obedient; for I may take it before that, not after it.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿قَالَ عِفْرِيتٌ مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ he is the strong, mighty one ﴿أَنَا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَقُومَ مِنْ مَقَامِكَ﴾ in which you sit to judge, which is from early morning until midday ﴿وَإِنِّي عَلَيْهِ لَقَوِيٌّ﴾ i.e. to carry it ﴿أَمِينٌ﴾ i.e. over the jewels and other things on it. Solomon said: I want [it] faster than that.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿قَالَ الَّذِي عِنْدَهُ عِلْمٌ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the revealed [Book]; he was Āṣaf ibn Barkhiyā, a man of truth (ṣiddīq) who knew the Greatest Name of Allah, by which, when He is called upon, He answers ﴿أَنَا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ﴾ when you look with it at something. So he said to him: Look at the sky. He looked at it, then turned his gaze back and found it placed before him. While he was looking at the sky, Āṣaf called upon the Greatest Name that Allah bring it, and this came about by its travelling beneath the earth until it sprang up beneath Solomon's chair ﴿فَلَمَّا رَآهُ مُسْتَقِرًّا﴾ i.e. still ﴿عِنْدَهُ قَالَ هَذَا﴾ i.e. its being brought to me ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِ رَبِّي لِيَبْلُوَنِي﴾ to test me ﴿أَأَشْكُرُ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully (taḥqīq), with the second changed into an alif, with it softened (tashīl), and with an alif inserted between the softened one and the other, or without it ﴿أَمْ أَكْفُرُ﴾ the blessing ﴿وَمَنْ شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ i.e. for its sake, because the reward of his thanks is his ﴿وَمَنْ كَفَرَ﴾ the blessing ﴿فَإِنَّ رَبِّي غَنِيٌّ﴾ in no need of his thanks ﴿كَرِيمٌ﴾ in bestowing favour on whoever is ungrateful for it.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿قَالَ نَكِّرُوا لَهَا عَرْشَهَا﴾ i.e. alter it to a state in which she will not recognise it when she sees it ﴿نَنْظُرْ أَتَهْتَدِي﴾ to recognising it ﴿أَمْ تَكُونُ مِنَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ to recognising what is altered for them. By this he intended to test her intelligence, because he had been told there was something [wrong] in it. So they altered it by adding, removing and so on.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَتْ قِيلَ﴾ to her ﴿أَهَكَذَا عَرْشُكِ﴾ i.e. is your throne like this? ﴿قَالَتْ كَأَنَّهُ هُوَ﴾ i.e. she recognised it, but made it ambiguous for them as they had made it ambiguous for her, since he did not say "Is this your throne?"; had that been said, she would have said "Yes". Solomon said, when he saw that she had recognition and knowledge: ﴿وَأُوتِينَا الْعِلْمَ مِنْ قَبْلِهَا وَكُنَّا مُسْلِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿وَصَدَّهَا﴾ from the worship of Allah ﴿مَا كَانَتْ تَعْبُدُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ مِنْ قَوْمٍ كَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿قِيلَ لَهَا﴾ also ﴿ادْخُلِي الصَّرْحَ﴾ it was a floor of clear white glass beneath which ran sweet water with fish in it; Solomon had made it when he was told that her shins and feet were like the feet of a donkey ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ حَسِبَتْهُ لُجَّةً﴾ of water ﴿وَكَشَفَتْ عَنْ سَاقَيْهَا﴾ to wade through it. Solomon was on his throne at the head of the hall, and he saw that her shins and feet were beautiful ﴿قَالَ﴾ to her ﴿إِنَّهُ صَرْحٌ مُمَرَّدٌ﴾ made smooth ﴿مِنْ قَوَارِيرَ﴾ i.e. of glass; and he called her to Islam ﴿قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي﴾ by worshipping other than You ﴿وَأَسْلَمْتُ﴾ being ﴿مَعَ سُلَيْمَانَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾. He wanted to marry her but disliked the hair on her shins, so the devils made a depilatory (nūra) for him and she removed it with it; so he married her, loved her and confirmed her in her kingdom. He used to visit her once every month and stay with her for three days, and her kingdom ended with the end of Solomon's kingdom. It is related that he became king at the age of thirteen and died at the age of fifty-three. So glory be to Him whose everlasting kingdom has no end.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَى ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ﴾ from the tribe ﴿صَالِحًا أَنِ﴾ i.e. bi-an ("that") ﴿اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ﴾ affirm His oneness ﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ فَرِيقَانِ يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾ about religion: one party believers from the time he was sent to them, and one party disbelievers.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ to those who denied ﴿يَا قَوْمِ لِمَ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ﴾ i.e. the punishment before mercy, in that you said: "If what you have brought us is true, then bring us the punishment" ﴿لَوْلَا﴾ why not ﴿تَسْتَغْفِرُونَ اللَّهَ﴾ for associating partners ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ﴾ and so not be punished.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿قَالُوا اطَّيَّرْنَا﴾ its original form is taṭayyarnā; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ and the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was brought in: we augur ill ﴿بِكَ وَبِمَنْ مَعَكَ﴾ i.e. the believers, since they suffered drought and hunger ﴿قَالَ طَائِرُكُمْ﴾ your ill omen ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ He brought it upon you ﴿بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ تُفْتَنُونَ﴾ you are being tested with good and evil.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَكَانَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ﴾ the city of Thamūd ﴿تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍ﴾ i.e. men ﴿يُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ with acts of disobedience, among them their clipping of dinars and dirhams ﴿وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ﴾ by obedience.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ i.e. they said to one another ﴿تَقَاسَمُوا﴾ i.e. swear ﴿بِاللَّهِ لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ﴾ with nūn, and with tāʾ with ḍamma on the second tāʾ ﴿وَأَهْلَهُ﴾ i.e. those who believed in him; i.e. we will kill them by night ﴿ثُمَّ لَنَقُولَنَّ﴾ with nūn, and with tāʾ with ḍamma on the second lām ﴿لِوَلِيِّهِ﴾ i.e. to the avenger of his blood ﴿مَا شَهِدْنَا﴾ we were not present at ﴿مُهْلَكَ أَهْلِهِ﴾ with ḍamma on the mīm and with fatḥa [مَهْلَكَ], i.e. their being destroyed or their perishing, so we do not know who killed them ﴿وَإِنَّا لَصَادِقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَمَكَرُوا﴾ in that ﴿مَكْرًا وَمَكَرْنَا مَكْرًا﴾ i.e. We requited them by hastening their punishment ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ﴾ We destroyed them ﴿وَقَوْمَهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ by the shout of Gabriel, or by the angels pelting them with stones which they could see while not seeing the angels.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خَاوِيَةً﴾ i.e. empty; it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the governing element (ʿāmil) in it is the meaning of the demonstrative ﴿بِمَا ظَلَمُوا﴾ because of their wrongdoing, i.e. their disbelief ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً﴾ a lesson ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ Our power, and so take admonition.

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿وَأَنْجَيْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ in Ṣāliḥ, and they were four thousand ﴿وَكَانُوا يَتَّقُونَ﴾ associating partners.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿وَلُوطًا﴾ accusative by an implied "remember" (udhkur) before it, and from it is substituted (badal): ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ أَتَأْتُونَ الْفَاحِشَةَ﴾ i.e. sodomy ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ i.e. you see one another, being absorbed in disobedience.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿أَئِنَّكُمْ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully and with the second softened, and with an alif inserted between them in both ways ﴿لَتَأْتُونَ الرِّجَالَ شَهْوَةً مِنْ دُونِ النِّسَاءِ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ﴾ the consequence of your deed.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا أَخْرِجُوا آلَ لُوطٍ﴾ his family ﴿مِنْ قَرْيَتِكُمْ إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ﴾ from the backsides of men.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُ وَأَهْلَهُ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَهُ قَدَّرْنَاهَا﴾ We made her, by Our decree ﴿مِنَ الْغَابِرِينَ﴾ of those remaining in the punishment.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مَطَرًا﴾ it was stones of baked clay (sijjīl), which destroyed them ﴿فَسَاءَ﴾ evil was ﴿مَطَرُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ﴾ with punishment — their rain.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿قُلِ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ﴾ for the destruction of the disbelievers of the past nations ﴿وَسَلَامٌ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَى﴾ them ﴿آللَّهُ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully, with the second changed into an alif [آللَّهُ], with it softened, and with an alif inserted between the softened one and the other, or without it ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ for whoever worships Him ﴿أَمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ [يُشْرِكُونَ], i.e. [what] the people of Mecca associate with Him — the gods — [are they] better for those who worship them? They asked him about the time of the coming of the Hour, and the following was revealed:

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿أَمَّنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَأَنْزَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَنْبَتْنَا﴾ in it there is iltifāt (a shift of person) from the third person to the first ﴿بِهِ حَدَائِقَ﴾ plural of ḥadīqa, which is a walled garden ﴿ذَاتَ بَهْجَةٍ﴾ beauty ﴿مَا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تُنْبِتُوا شَجَرَهَا﴾ because you have no power to do so ﴿أَإِلَهٌ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully and with the second softened, and with an alif inserted between them in both ways, in its seven occurrences ﴿مَعَ اللَّهِ﴾ who helped Him in that? i.e. there is no god with Him ﴿بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ يَعْدِلُونَ﴾ they associate others with Allah.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿أَمَّنْ جَعَلَ الْأَرْضَ قَرَارًا﴾ which does not sway with its inhabitants ﴿وَجَعَلَ خِلَالَهَا﴾ in between it ﴿أَنْهَارًا وَجَعَلَ لَهَا رَوَاسِيَ﴾ mountains by which He made the earth firm ﴿وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ حَاجِزًا﴾ between the fresh and the salt, so that neither mixes with the other ﴿أَإِلَهٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ His oneness.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿أَمَّنْ يُجِيبُ الْمُضْطَرَّ﴾ the distressed one who has been touched by harm ﴿إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكْشِفُ السُّوءَ﴾ from him and from others ﴿وَيَجْعَلُكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ the iḍāfa (genitive construct) is in the sense of "in", i.e. every generation succeeds the generation before it ﴿أَإِلَهٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ قَلِيلًا مَا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ you take heed; with the upper-dotted [tāʾ] and the lower-dotted [yāʾ], and in it the tāʾ is assimilated into the dhāl, and mā is redundant (zāʾida), to make the little even less [تَذَكَّرُونَ].

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿أَمَّنْ يَهْدِيكُمْ﴾ guides you to your destinations ﴿فِي ظُلُمَاتِ الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ﴾ by the stars at night and by landmarks by day ﴿وَمَنْ يُرْسِلُ الرِّيَاحَ بُشْرًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ i.e. ahead of the rain ﴿أَإِلَهٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ with Him of others.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿أَمَّنْ يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ﴾ in the wombs from a drop of sperm ﴿ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾ after death, even if they do not acknowledge the restoration, since proofs of it have been established ﴿وَمَنْ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾ with rain ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ with plants ﴿أَإِلَهٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. none does any of what has been mentioned except Allah, and there is no god with Him ﴿قُلْ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ﴾ your proof ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ that there is a god with me who did any of what has been mentioned. [Translator's note: «مَعِي» "with me" is as in the source; «مَعَهُ» "with Him" would be expected.]

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿قُلْ لَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ of angels and people ﴿الْغَيْبَ﴾ what is hidden from them ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but (lākin) ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ knows it ﴿وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca, like others ﴿أَيَّانَ﴾ the time when ﴿يُبْعَثُونَ﴾

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ in the sense of hal ﴿أَدْرَكَ﴾ on the pattern of akrama; in another reading [ادَّارَكَ] with a doubled dāl, whose original form is tadāraka: the tāʾ was changed into a dāl and assimilated into the dāl, and the connecting hamza was brought in; i.e. it reached and caught up, or followed in succession ﴿عِلْمُهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾ i.e. about it, so that they asked about the time of its coming? The matter is not so ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْهَا بَلْ هُمْ مِنْهَا عَمُونَ﴾ from blindness of the heart, and this is more emphatic than what precedes it. The original form is ʿamiyūna: the ḍamma was found heavy on the yāʾ, so it was transferred to the mīm after its kasra was dropped.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ also, in denial of the resurrection ﴿أَإِذَا كُنَّا تُرَابًا وَآبَاؤُنَا أَئِنَّا لَمُخْرَجُونَ﴾ from the graves.

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿لَقَدْ وُعِدْنَا هَذَا نَحْنُ وَآبَاؤُنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنْ﴾ i.e. not (mā) ﴿هَذَا إِلَّا أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ plural of usṭūra, with ḍamma, i.e. lies that have been written down.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ through denying it, and that was their destruction by punishment.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا تَكُنْ فِي ضَيْقٍ مِمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ﴾ a consolation for the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. do not be concerned about their plotting against you, for We will give you victory over them.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَى هَذَا الْوَعْدُ﴾ of punishment ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ about it.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿قُلْ عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونَ رَدِفَ﴾ drawn near ﴿لَكُمْ بَعْضُ الَّذِي تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾ and so killing befell them at Badr, and the rest of the punishment will come to them after death.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ﴾ part of which is postponing the punishment from the disbelievers ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾ for the disbelievers do not give thanks for the postponement of the punishment, because they deny that it will happen.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَعْلَمُ مَا تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمْ﴾ conceal ﴿وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ﴾ with their tongues.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿وَمَا مِنْ غَائِبَةٍ فِي السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ the hāʾ [i.e. tāʾ marbūṭa] is for intensification (mubālagha), i.e. anything utterly hidden from people ﴿إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ clear, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ), and in His hidden knowledge, exalted is He; part of that is the punishment of the disbelievers.

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَقُصُّ عَلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ those living in the time of our Prophet ﴿أَكْثَرَ الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ i.e. by setting out what has been mentioned in its true form, which would remove the disagreement among them if they adopted it and became Muslims.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَهُدًى﴾ from misguidance ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ from punishment.

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ like others, on the Day of Resurrection ﴿بِحُكْمِهِ﴾ i.e. His justice ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ the Overpowering ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what He judges, so no one can oppose Him, as the disbelievers opposed His prophets in this world.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ trust in Him ﴿إِنَّكَ عَلَى الْحَقِّ الْمُبِينِ﴾ i.e. the clear religion, so the final outcome is yours, with victory over the disbelievers. Then He struck likenesses for them with the dead, the deaf and the blind, and said:

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿إِنَّكَ لَا تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتَى وَلَا تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ الدُّعَاءَ إِذَا﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully and with the second softened between it and yāʾ ﴿وَلَّوْا مُدْبِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿وَمَا أَنْتَ بِهَادِي الْعُمْيِ عَنْ ضَلَالَتِهِمْ إِنْ﴾ i.e. not (mā) ﴿تُسْمِعُ﴾ a hearing of understanding and acceptance ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ the Qurʾan ﴿فَهُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ sincere in affirming the oneness of Allah.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَإِذَا وَقَعَ الْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ the punishment is due to descend upon them among the totality of the disbelievers ﴿أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾ i.e. it will speak to those alive at the time of its emergence, in Arabic, saying to them, among the rest of its speech, on Our behalf: ﴿أَنَّ النَّاسَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca; and on the reading with fatḥa on the hamza of anna, a bāʾ is implied after تُكَلِّمُهُمْ ﴿كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا لَا يُوقِنُونَ﴾ do not believe in the Qurʾan, which includes the resurrection, the reckoning and the punishment. With its emergence, commanding good and forbidding evil comes to an end, and no disbeliever will believe, just as Allah revealed to Noah: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed."

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿يَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ فَوْجًا﴾ a group ﴿مِمَّنْ يُكَذِّبُ بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ and they are their leaders who were followed ﴿فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ﴾ they are gathered, by the last of them being brought back to the first, then driven along.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءُوا﴾ the place of reckoning ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted, to them ﴿أَكَذَّبْتُمْ﴾ My prophets ﴿بِآيَاتِي وَلَمْ تُحِيطُوا﴾ on account of your denial ﴿بِهَا عِلْمًا أَمَّا﴾ in it the interrogative mā is assimilated ﴿ذَا﴾ a relative noun, i.e. "what is it that" ﴿كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ of what you were commanded?

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿وَوَقَعَ الْقَوْلُ﴾ the punishment became due ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ بِمَا ظَلَمُوا﴾ i.e. associated partners ﴿فَهُمْ لَا يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ since they have no argument.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا﴾ created ﴿اللَّيْلَ لِيَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ﴾ like others ﴿وَالنَّهَارَ مُبْصِرًا﴾ in the sense of "in which one sees", so that they may go about their affairs in it ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ﴾ indications of His power, exalted is He ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ they are singled out for mention because they benefit from them in faith, unlike the disbelievers.

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ﴾ the horn, the first blowing, by Isrāfīl ﴿فَفَزِعَ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ they fear with a fear that leads to death, as in another verse: «فَصَعِقَ»; the past tense is used in it because its occurrence is certain ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. Gabriel, Michael, Isrāfīl and the Angel of Death; and from Ibn ʿAbbās: they are the martyrs, since they are alive with their Lord, provided for ﴿وَكُلٌّ﴾ its nunation is a substitute for the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive), i.e. and all of them, after being brought back to life on the Day of Resurrection ﴿أَتَوْهُ﴾ in the form of the verb and of the active participle ﴿دَاخِرِينَ﴾ humbled; the past tense is used for the coming because its occurrence is certain.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿وَتَرَى الْجِبَالَ﴾ you see them at the time of the blowing ﴿تَحْسَبُهَا﴾ you think them ﴿جَامِدَةً﴾ standing still in their place because of their hugeness ﴿وَهِيَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحَابِ﴾ rain [clouds] when the wind strikes them, i.e. they move as they move until they fall to the earth and become level with it, scattered; then they become like carded wool, then scattered dust ﴿صُنْعَ اللَّهِ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising the content of the clause before it, annexed to its agent after its governing verb was omitted, i.e. Allah made that a making ﴿الَّذِي أَتْقَنَ﴾ perfected ﴿كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ He made ﴿إِنَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تَفْعَلُونَ], i.e. His enemies, of disobedience, and His friends, of obedience.

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ﴾ i.e. "there is no god but Allah", on the Day of Resurrection ﴿فَلَهُ خَيْرٌ﴾ reward ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ i.e. because of it; it is not for comparison (tafḍīl), since there is no deed better than it; and in another verse: «عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا» ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ those who bring it ﴿مِنْ فَزَعِ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ with iḍāfa (genitive construct) and with kasra or fatḥa on the mīm, and with فَزَع nunated and fatḥa on the mīm [فَزَعٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ] ﴿آمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿وَمَنْ جَاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ﴾ i.e. associating partners ﴿فَكُبَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِي النَّارِ﴾ in that they are turned towards it; faces are mentioned because they are the noblest place of the senses, so the rest is all the more so. And it will be said to them in rebuke: ﴿هَلْ﴾ i.e. not (mā) ﴿تُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا﴾ the recompense of ﴿مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ of associating partners and acts of disobedience. Say to them:

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ رَبَّ هَذِهِ الْبَلْدَةِ﴾ i.e. Mecca ﴿الَّذِي حَرَّمَهَا﴾ i.e. made it a safe sanctuary, in which human blood is not shed, no one is wronged, its game is not hunted and its fresh herbage is not cut; and that is among the blessings upon Quraysh, its people, in Allah's removing from their land the punishment and the trials that were widespread in all the lands of the Arabs ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ the Exalted ﴿كُلُّ شَيْءٍ﴾ so He is its Lord, Creator and Owner ﴿وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾ to Allah, by affirming His oneness.

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿وَأَنْ أَتْلُوَ الْقُرْآنَ﴾ to you, a recitation calling to faith ﴿فَمَنِ اهْتَدَى﴾ by it ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ i.e. for its sake, for the reward of his being guided is his ﴿وَمَنْ ضَلَّ﴾ from faith and missed the path of guidance ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ to him ﴿إِنَّمَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُنْذِرِينَ﴾ the warners, so nothing is upon me but conveying [the message]; and this was before the command to fight.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿وَقُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ سَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ فَتَعْرِفُونَهَا﴾ and Allah showed them on the day of Badr killing, captivity and the angels striking their faces and backs, and Allah hastened them to the Fire ﴿وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تَعْمَلُونَ]; He only grants them respite until their appointed time.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿طس﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ i.e. these verses ﴿آيَاتُ الْقُرْآنِ﴾ verses of it ﴿وَكِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ which makes the truth distinct from falsehood — a conjunction (ʿaṭf) with the addition of an attribute; it is

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿هُدًى﴾ i.e. guiding from error ﴿وَبُشْرَى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ who believe in it — [good news] of Paradise.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ﴾ perform it in its proper manner ﴿وَيُؤْتُونَ﴾ give ﴿الزَّكَوةَ وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ﴾ know it by reasoning from evidence; and هُمْ is repeated because of what separated it from the khabar (predicate).

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ زَيَّنَّا لَهُمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ ugly, by implanting desire, so that they saw them as good ﴿فَهُمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾ wander in confusion, because of their ugliness in Our sight.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ الْعَذَابِ﴾ its most severe, in this world: killing and captivity ﴿وَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ هُمُ الْأَخْسَرُونَ﴾ because they end up in the Fire, everlasting for them.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَإِنَّكَ﴾ an address to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿لَتُلَقَّى الْقُرْآنَ﴾ i.e. it is cast upon you with force ﴿مِنْ لَدُنْ﴾ from ﴿حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾ in that. Remember

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِأَهْلِهِ﴾ his wife, during his journey from Madyan to Egypt ﴿إِنِّي آنَسْتُ﴾ I have seen from afar ﴿نَارًا سَآتِيكُمْ مِنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ﴾ about the state of the road — he had lost it ﴿أَوْ آتِيكُمْ بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ﴾ with iḍāfa (genitive construct) for explanation (bayān), and without it [بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ], i.e. a flame of fire at the tip of a wick or a stick ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ﴾ and the ṭāʾ is a substitute for the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form, from صَلِيَ بِالنَّارِ, with kasra and fatḥa on the lām: that you may warm yourselves against the cold.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهَا نُودِيَ أَنْ﴾ i.e. بِأَنْ ﴿بُورِكَ﴾ i.e. Allah has blessed ﴿مَنْ فِي النَّارِ﴾ i.e. Mūsā ﴿وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا﴾ i.e. the angels — or the reverse; and بَارَكَ is transitive by itself and by the preposition; and after فِي, مَكَان (place) is implied ﴿وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ part of what was called out, and its meaning is declaring Allah free of evil.
